Table 1: Main results on the LaMP benchmark under the time-based split. Each cell reports the dev-set metric for one (task, metric) pair under a given user-representation baseline; all methods share the same LoRA-SFT pipeline, so the textual prefix prepended to the input is the only point of variation across columns. Best per-row result in bold; second best underlined. All numbers are averaged over 3 random seeds.
Table 2: Ablation on the bidirectional reward.

Table 10: Complementarity of self-supervised and tasksupervised rewards. The combined reward (right column) wins on every row. Best per-row result in bold.

Figure 11: Training dynamics of the bidirectional reward across the six LaMP tasks. Each column shows one task; the top row plots Rfwd (blue) and the bottom row plots Rbwd (red). Light traces are the raw per-step mean; bold curves apply an EWMA smoother (α=0.1). Y-axes are scaled independently per subplot to highlight relative motion. Both directions rise monotonically on every task, confirming that the bidirectional reward delivers usable gradient throughout training.

Figure 9: Zero-shot Gemini profile-generation prompts. The only systematic difference from the BUMP prompt of Figure 8 is the explicit “(2–3 sentences)” length constraint, which substitutes for the soft length penalty Rlen that BUMP applies during GRPO — the Gemini API baselines are not trained, so no learned length control is available.
